      <title>Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b</link>
      <description><p>Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’</p><p>The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.</p><p>It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/missed-opportunity-guinea-bissaus-children-why-trial-frederik-wttde/">wrote</a> on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau</link>
      <description><p>Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns</p><p>Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials <a href="https://www.facebook.com/policiajudiciariaguinebissau/posts/pfbid02x8etNUtmPjenMNZA69EHECDBcz6U4VzxTvszdthBmFmJ1aaCMwoT9brgRNYyg1Jbl">said</a> on Facebook.</p><p>The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:44:48 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>‘No change’ in Russia’s attitude on war shown by deadly attacks, Zelensky says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261022-no-change-russia-attitude-war-after-deadly-attacks-zelensky-says</link><description>
Russia’s latest attacks on Ukraine show there has been “no real change” in Moscow’s attitude towards the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday. The deadly strikes came just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff his country was ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington and Kyiv.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2ea45b56-c7f7-11f1-a634-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3AQ7YY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2ea45b56-c7f7-11f1-a634-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3AQ7YY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e072897c-ce35-11f1-824a-9b6d5f985417</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:43:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2ea45b56-c7f7-11f1-a634-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3AQ7YY.jpg">© Henry Nicholls, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/ahead-of-us-and-israeli-elections-3-day-joint-attack-on-iran-would-not-radically-change-conflict</link><description>
Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Federico Donelli, Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the University of Trieste in Italy. Can another three days of military strikes achieve what eight months of confrontation have failed to deliver? Donelli challenges the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would necessarily produce a decisive political outcome. He argues, "the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran's capacity, or to pressure Iran to sit on the table." And whether they can translate that capacity into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. Regardless, Donelli reminds us that "Iran still has leverage over the US."
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c66a7ce-ce2d-11f1-9d8f-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261022-152144-153307-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c66a7ce-ce2d-11f1-9d8f-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261022-152144-153307-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">620ff428-ce2d-11f1-8eed-af0e081df335</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:36:26 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴Live: Authorities in Lyon and Marseille ban all protests Saturday</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261022-live-paris-bans-protests-after-violent-unrest-as-macron-takes-swipe-at-trump</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">0e43b4b0-ce32-11f1-9f5b-abfb5f60efb6</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:03:29 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French shopkeepers fear new looting in upcoming protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/french-shopkeepers-fear-new-looting-in-upcoming-protests</link><description>
In Paris, shopkeepers fear further losses ahead of a demonstration planned for next Saturday. After last weekend’s protests saw scenes of vandalism, some are considering closing their shops, while others plan to stay open.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d62805ac-ce2e-11f1-9a82-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-Thumbnail-4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d62805ac-ce2e-11f1-9a82-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-Thumbnail-4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f277d5de-ce2e-11f1-8fd5-7bedae330559</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:51:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes after US envoy visit to the Kremlin</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/ukraine-and-russia-exchange-strikes-after-us-envoy-visit-to-the-kremlin</link><description>
Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone and missile strikes on Thursday, killing seven people in Ukraine, according to authorities. Moscow said it had intercepted 630 Ukrainian drones targeting the Russian capital. The strikes came hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Witkoff said Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/227bc5ce-ce2f-11f1-afee-7967b15eed96/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-Thumbnail-1-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/227bc5ce-ce2f-11f1-afee-7967b15eed96/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-Thumbnail-1-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">44f35ca2-ce2f-11f1-9d0b-05a7896dd38a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:50:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description>A federal judge on Thursday ordered US President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC by December 11.
The order from US Magistrate Judge Enjolique Lett came as lawyers for the British broadcaster complained that Trump had delayed his appearance.
Charles Tobin, the lawyer for the BBC, said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff”.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:14:56 +0000 en <![CDATA[ 'Cabin leak suspected': Artemis II astronaut reveals how a warning nearly derailed NASA's epic moon mission ]]> TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — NASA's Artemis II astronauts were just minutes away from a critical engine burn that would send them toward the moon when an unexpected cabin leak warning threatened to change the course of their historic mission.

"If it had happened five minutes later, we may not have been able to have that burn," Artemis II pilot Victor Glover revealed during an Oct. 18 discussion with Canadian former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival here in Tenerife.

The incident unfolded on April 2, the second day of the Artemis II mission, as the astronauts' Orion spacecraft swooped back toward Earth after traveling some 38,000 miles (61,000 kilometers) away. Orion had been completing a highly elliptical orbit around Earth, giving the crew and mission control an opportunity to test the capsule's systems before committing to the journey to the moon. Orion was now approaching its closest point to our planet, roughly 100 miles (160 km) above the surface, ahead of the crucial translunar injection (TLI) burn that would send the astronauts moonward.

"Jeremy looks out the window and says, 'I think we're going to run smack dab into the middle of Earth,'" Glover recalled, referring to Artemis II mission specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency. "Because we were getting so low."

The close approach brought additional challenges, as Orion passed through a region populated by orbital debris and satellites.

"The density of things is going up from where we are, and also an increase in radiation," Glover explained.

It was at this particularly demanding point in the mission that Orion issued a warning that indicated a possible cabin leak, around 15 minutes before the critical TLI burn.

"So, determining whether it was real or not was a big deal," Glover said.

The crew and mission control faced a crucial question: Was it safe to continue heading to the moon, or would they have to abandon the planned maneuver and cut the mission very short? "Are we going to do a TLI and burn to go to the moon, or are we putting on our spacesuits to prepare to come back to Earth right now?" Glover recalled.

The timing was particularly critical. The TLI burn was designed to propel Orion out of Earth orbit and onto its trajectory around the moon, marking the first time astronauts had headed toward Earth's nearest neighbor since the Apollo era.

Luckily, as NASA flight director Judd Frieling told us during an April 2 media briefing, the warning turned out to be a false alarm.

So Artemis II received the go-ahead. Orion fired its main engine for approximately five minutes and 50 seconds, successfully setting the four astronauts on their journey around the moon.

"We're watching the timer count down, velocities go up, and the magenta and green numbers coming together," Glover recalled.

"Everything is tracking. It's looking good."

Before long, the crew had broken free of Earth's gravitational hold and were hurtling toward the moon at around 24,500 mph (39,430 kph).

Despite the tense moments before the burn, Artemis II went on to make history. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (the mission's commander), Glover (pilot) and Christina Koch (mission specialist), along with Hansen, traveled farther from Earth than any humans before them, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) during their journey around the moon.

The four astronauts returned safely to Earth on April 10, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego after nearly 10 days in space.

]]> <![CDATA[ Australia's bizarre 'Spider Crater' seen from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 22, 2026 ]]>

From the dangerous Sydney funnel-web to the common huntsman, Australia is home to its fair share of spiders. It even has a crater shaped like one.

What is it?

One stretch of the vast Western Australia wilderness is imprinted with a curious crater, which likely formed after a meteor impact hundreds of millions of years ago. Geologists think the spider-like pattern in the crater's center was created when its floor rebounded following the initial impact, NASA has said.

In the hundreds of millions of years since the initial impact, erosion has continued to carve this formation into its current, signature shape. Complete with "legs," the planetary imprint has earned its name Spider Crater.

This image shows the impact structure in its entirety, which stretches 8 by 7 miles (13 by 11 kilometers) in full, with the central "spider" piece measuring 2.5 miles (4 km).

Why is it incredible?

In this image, we can see this "spider" from space. This snapshot shows the geologic feature as captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) aboard the Landsat 9 satellite, an Earth-observing craft that launched back in 2021.

The satellite, a collaborative effort between NASA and the U.S. Geological Survey, is the ninth in the Landsat Earth-observing series, which goes all the way back to the launch of Landsat 1 in 1972. On a near-weekly basis, Landsat 9 delivers observations of everything from deforestation to water quality and crop growth.

The series of Landsat satellites have been a critical piece in the modern understanding of how our planet continues to change. Whether it's the repercussions of climate change or fluctuations in agriculture, observations from orbit do more than provide interesting photos of our home world; they also capture critical data.

]]> <![CDATA[ Next Mass Effect game cancelled as EA shuts down legendary sci-fi RPG studio BioWare ]]> The writing was on the wall, but the news still hit us like a truck yesterday. BioWare, the iconic RPG studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age series, is no more. Development on the next Mass Effect has stopped, but EA might not be entirely done with the IP.

Variety reported, backed by EA’s own statement and BioWare’s goodbye on socials, that EA is laying off 3% of its global workforce and closing down BioWare. The shift comes shortly after the company went fully private this summer, with Saudi Arabia and private equity acquiring it alongside all its studios and properties.

A new Mass Effect game — meant to serve as a follow-up to the original trilogy — had been in development since the early 2020s, though progress was slow following severe downsizing after 2024’s Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA’s expectations. According to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, only around 50 staff remained at the studio, which would’ve needed to go on a hiring spree to complete development of the massive sci-fi RPG.

The first post-shutdown shocker arrived a bit later, with IGN exclusively revealing that Mass Effect isn't entirely dead, as the upcoming live-action TV show based on Mass Effect is still moving forward at Prime Video.

The series started active development at Amazon in late 2024, but it has yet to reach production status. Little is known about the story, but rumors point to it aiming to bridge the gap between the original trilogy and the now-cancelled new game. Despite closing the studio that created it, EA still owns the Mass Effect property.

Variety’s report, which includes more comments from EA’s top brass about the present and future of the publisher, also contains updates on Marvel’s Iron Man (developed at Motive) and Star Wars Jedi 3 (Respawn Entertainment). Both are still coming, and the more surprising news comes in the shape of DICE and Respawn teaming up for a totally new project, believed to be Star Wars Battlefront 3 after days of strong rumors from a number of reputable sources.

Elsewhere, ex-BioWare developers have teamed up at new studios like Archetype and Arcanaut. The former is preparing to ship Mass Effect-inspired action RPG Exodus in 2027, and the latter recently started work on Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, with original Knights of the Old Republic (and Mass Effect) director Casey Hudson behind the wheel.

Here’s hoping both studios, as well as the recently laid-off developers, can find success in an increasingly hostile industry.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA giving update about Artemis moon plans on Oct. 23: Watch it live ]]>

NASA will provide an update about its Artemis moon plans on Friday (Oct. 23), and you can watch it live.

The news will come during a press conference at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, which starts Friday at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA.

"The update will include details about NASA’s Artemis III mission that will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings, and how plans to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 are progressing," NASA officials said in an Oct. 14 media advisory.

Three agency officials will participate in Friday's "Artemis Acceleration" event. They are:

  • NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
  • NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya
  • Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager

NASA is currently gearing up for Artemis III, which is targeted for mid-2027. The mission will test rendezvous and docking technologies between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the private spacecraft that NASA picked to be the Artemis program's crewed lunar landers: SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.

After that will come Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the lunar south pole in early 2028, if all goes to plan. That will be the first crewed moon touchdown since Apollo 17 way back in 1972.

It's unclear which lunar lander will fly on Artemis IV; that depends on how the development of each one progresses and what happens on Artemis III.

And there will be other landings after Artemis IV. NASA plans to establish a moon base via Artemis, and doing so will require a variety of missions, both robotic and crewed.

The agency feels some urgency in this quest, for China has similar goals. It's important that the U.S. wins this new space race, military and political officials have said, so that the nation can establish the norms of responsible behavior on Earth's nearest neighbor.

"The update will include details about NASA’s Artemis III mission that will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings, and how plans to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 are progressing," NASA officials said in an Oct. 14 media advisory.

  • NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya
  • Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1 ]]>

On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor.

Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.)

It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year. The mission ended abruptly 14 months ahead of its planned end date when scientists lost contact with the probe.

Why it mattered

The Indian Space Research Organisation, or ISRO, had a lot riding on the success of Chandrayaan-1 moon mission, which marked the first-ever deep space mission by the Indian space agency. It was also the first mission to the moon for India, a country that hopes to launch its own crewed spacecraft and build a space station.

Chandrayaan-1 did more than just demonstrate that India's space program was capable of launching missions to the moon; it also returned some amazing science results, like evidence of water ice on the moon.

"In September 2009, scientists published results of data collected by the American M3 instrument which had detected absorption features on the polar regions of the surface of the Moon usually linked to hydroxyl- and/ or water-bearing molecules," NASA said in a mission overview.

The spacecraft carried 11 instruments to study the moon, five of them built by ISRO. The rest were experiments for the European Space Agnecy and NASA.

"In addition to the five Indian instruments, the spacecraft carried scientific equipment from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, and Bulgaria," NASA said.

It took until Nov. 8, 2008 for Chandrayaan-1 to enter lunar orbit, where it stayed until contact was lost in August 2009, most likely due to a power supply failure caused by overheating.

"This was short of the spacecraft’s planned two-year lifetime, although ISRO noted that at least 95% of its mission objectives had been accomplished by then," NASA wrote.

India did not stop at the moon with Chandrayaan-1. In 2019, the country launched the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which carried the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. Chandrayaan-2 reached lunar orbit successfully, but the Vikram landing failed.

The Chandrayaan-3 misson followed in 2023, which successfully landed a new Vikram lander and Pragyan rover near the moon's south pole. India plans to launch the Chandryaan-4 mission to return moon samples to Earth in 2028.

]]> <![CDATA[ Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview) ]]> Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, "Lost on Paradise", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week.

Foster famously ghost-wrote the first "Star Wars" novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.

In addition to crafting the screen story for "Star Trek: The Motion Picture," Foster also wrote the novelizations for the first three "Alien" films, Disney's "The Black Hole," John Carpenter's "The Thing," "The Last Starfighter," "Star Trek," "Transformers," "Terminator: Salvation", and many more.

Lost on Paradise by Alan Dean Foster: $19.99
New York Times bestselling author Alan Dean Foster, master of both action and emotion, reveals a world where everything is perfect, but nothing is as it seems…View Deal

The near-future, off-world escapades of "Lost On Paradise" are the latest addition to Foster’s acclaimed bounty of bestselling standalone novels and series, including the popular "Spellsinger" series.

"Earth is crowded, polluted, and dismal," states the novel's synopsis. "Like millions of others, Jonos and Liina scrape by on her poorly paying job and what little money he gets selling items scavenged from rich people’s trash. Like millions of others, Jonos and Liina dream of Paradise.

"Paradise: a beautiful, clean, verdant world where three races live in harmony—at least, according to the videos sent back to Earth. There are the Eiquan, masters of astonishing technology; the Lusanata, hunters and farmers; and humans, who may be restricted to a few scattered settlements, but still live a life ten times better than those on Earth.

"On the run after a criminal act, Jonos and Liina finally escape to Paradise. It's everything they hoped for. Until tragedy strikes."

The genesis of Foster's "Lost on Paradise" is something that’s been percolating in his fertile mind for many years.

"I had this notion of a planet called Paradise where everything is perfect, and everything on Earth is seriously messed up," Foster tells Space. "There’s this couple who have problems; they’re poor like everybody else.

"And you have a unique male protagonist because he recognizes that his female partner is smarter than him, so she’s the brains of the outfit, and he supplies the muscle. Although he's not stupid. Too often you get a big, hulking guy with no brains. But she has a potentially fatal disease, and they’re trying to get away like a lot of poor people in the world today. So here's a place called Paradise. How do you get there? It’s expensive and difficult. And what happens if they do? Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise."

In crafting a deteriorating New York some 150 years or so down the calendar, it was important to stay sharp regarding developments that pop up in the news to avoid any internal logic conflicts.

"You just don’t want to get caught out by a scientific development that you postulate is near future when it's actually contemporary," explains Foster. "So I was very careful with that. But as you’re building out an alien environment and one that’s supposed to be perfect and beautiful, and then there’s maybe some things about it that aren’t, what do you introduce to show that?

"You don’t want to contradict yourself when you’re worldbuilding. That's a large problem that’s unfortunately common in science fiction," notes Foster. "Where somebody is breathing air, and suddenly they’re breathing methane, and it just doesn’t work. There’s a lot of different variables that come together that prove that Paradise is Paradise in some ways and not in others. A good example would be when the first Europeans reached Tahiti. The problem was that the people who entered this Paradise brought venereal disease and smallpox, to which the Polynesians had no resistance. So it's Paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up."

Now enjoy our exclusive chapter excerpt from Alan Dean Foster’s "Lost On Paradise." Published by Blackstone Publishing.

Why shouldn’t a man and a woman in his and Liina’s position try to get to Paradise? Jonos mused as he treaded his way homeward. Though morning continued its ascent, the sun did not. Or so it seemed, when the omnipresent pollution often rendered day as dark as night. The gloom was useful for masking scavenging activities and for concealing one’s identity. It was less suitable for more plebian activities such as breathing and eating. Or living. Life on Earth sucked.

But on Paradise…

To emigrant humans it went without saying that Paradise was aptly named. Everyone had heard the stories. On Paradise a person could breathe freely. Without a mask, without fear of needing lung implants, without having to worry about inhaling a soupçon of strychnine or similar industrial pollutants. On Paradise food was plentiful and fresh, water devoid of contaminants. There was work, too, for anyone willing to adapt to entirely new surroundings, for those willing to acknowledge the much-talked-about overlordship of the dominant species. For arrivals willing to submit to the experimental, ever-evolving social structure, and to the limitations that were placed on newcomers, the technologically superior Eiquans professed an indifference that amounted to a willing welcome.

Or so the compendium of hugely diverse anecdotes insisted. That’s all they were, Jonos knew. Stories and speculation, rumors and conjecture. Ignoring the spotty rain that had begun to fall, he turned a corner and nearly ran over a couple who scrambled to get out of his way. The man he had accidentally jostled started to say something, quickly realized the size of the individual he was about to chastise, and mumbled on his way, dragging a woman—likely his wife—with him. Jonos paid them no mind. Half of him was engaged in navigating his way home, the other half in dreaming of what Paradise might actually be like.

In truth, he had never met anyone who had actually been to Paradise. He had never met anyone who knew anyone who had been to Paradise. That did not make the distant world any less real. The media periodically released vits and images of the place. These showed an Earth-like planet swathed in an atmosphere perfectly suitable for humans. The indigenous wildlife was fascinating, the few but thriving, improvised communities intriguing, and the rarely seen Eiquans themselves tall, gracile, and sophisticated. So what if they weren’t humanoid? They were bisymmetrical, anyway, highly intelligent, and by all accounts no worse than indifferent to the interests of other species. So beautiful and graceful was their slender physicality, so mellifluous their speech, that even though they were quite alien the idea of living among them held no fear for Jonos.

Anything, he knew, would be a step up from Earth.

Lost on Paradise by Alan Dean Foster: $19.99
New York Times bestselling author Alan Dean Foster, master of both action and emotion, reveals a world where everything is perfect, but nothing is as it seems…

]]> <![CDATA[ "A great budget lens for astrophotography, the sharpness produced at f/1.8 and f/2.8 is exactly what you want." Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens review ]]>
Key specs

Type: Full-frame prime lens

Focal length: 16mm

Maximum aperture: f/1.8

Lens mount: Sony FE, Nikon Z

Weight: 19.4 oz (550 g)

Dimensions: 3.35 x 4.06-in (85.2 x 103 mm)

Filter thread: 77 mm

Release date: May 2023

As you know, prime lenses come in a wide range of sizes and focal lengths, and every once in a while, one comes along and seems to grab you by the scruff of your neck. One such lens is the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE, which is an impressive and useful lens for astrophotography thanks to its wide-angle field of view and fast maximum aperture.

This lens is one of the wider prime lenses that are available and could be one of the best third-party lenses for astrophotography. With a price of just $464 (£533), this is one of the most cost-effective wide-angle primes, but rather than being a second-rate lens, its build quality and image quality are fantastic. It’s not the best, but it’s undoubtedly a lens you would enjoy.

Image quality is excellent overall, with no need for lens corrections, except for vignette removal when shooting wide open. With near-perfect sharpness and minimal distortion and aberrations straight out of the camera, perhaps the weight of the lens is a small price to pay.

The lens is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups and is built like a tank, with an all-metal body. It is pretty heavy, though, weighing in at 19.4 oz (550 g) despite its relatively compact size. Attach this lens to one of the best Sony cameras and you will have a formidable combination. The 16mm f/1.8 is also available in the Nikon Z-mount.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens review

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Performance

  • Great image quality
  • Impressively sharp at f/1.8
  • Excellent corner sharpness

With a focal length of 16mm and a maximum aperture of f/1.8, this is clearly a great lens for astrophotography from a technical point of view. The light-gathering capabilities are excellent, to say the least, and during testing it was possible to shoot at a range of ISO levels with a moonless sky. Even ISO 800 was often high enough for a correct exposure.

The image quality produced by the 16mm f/1.8 is great, with excellent levels of sharpness across the frame. What’s most important here is that even corner sharpness is fantastic when wide open at f/1.8. This is the aperture setting where vignetting is at its strongest, but it reduces drastically when you stop down to f/2.8 and is completely gone by the time you stop down to f/4.

Luckily, though, there is a lens profile in Adobe Camera Raw and Adobe Lightroom that completely removes vignetting. There’s also only minimal chromatic aberration and a tiny amount of barrel distortion, which is impressive given the wide field of view produced by the lens.

As mentioned before, sharpness is great wide open and improves incrementally as you stop down up to the sweet spot of the lens, which is f/8. Sharpness drops slightly at f/11, and it’s at f/16 where diffraction begins to soften the image overall. This increases further when you stop down to f/22.

These latter apertures aren’t relevant to astrophotography; the medium ones aren’t either but the sharpness produced at f/1.8 and f/2.8 is exactly what you want.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Design

  • Weather-sealed build
  • Compact yet heavy
  • Great handling

The 16mm f/1.8 lens is something of an oddity in one respect: it’s both compact and heavy considering its size, although this comes down to its optical construction. The lens weighs 19.4 oz (550 g) with a size of just 3.35 x 4.06 in (85.2 x 103 mm). It does, however, balance well with Sony A-series cameras.

The 16mm f/1.8 is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups, including four ED glass and three aspherical lenses. The optical construction is designed to deliver sharpness, detail and high contrast with minimal distortion. It’s fair to say it achieves these. Of course, you will experience some perspective distortion when tilting the lens up to capture more of the night sky when there are ground elements in the foreground.

Unlike some wide-angle lenses, the front element isn’t bulbous, and it features an HD nano multilayer coating with a water-resistant and antifouling coating. The filter thread is also just 77mm, so you can easily attach screw-in and square filters if you use them for your astrophotography.

The minimum focusing distance of the lens is 10.6 inches (27 cm), which is great for landscape photographers but less important for astrophotographers.

Build quality is impressive thanks to an all-metal body and weather-sealing. This gives the lens a premium look, and it feels robust in the hand. There’s also a useful digital color screen that displays lens information.

When it comes to controls, there are possibly a few more on this lens than you might find on the average prime. There’s a manual focusing ring that’s wide enough for use when wearing gloves, a manual aperture ring that can be set to stepped and stepless operation using a switch on one side of the lens, two customizable Fn buttons and an AF/MF switch.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Functionality

  • Small color digital screen
  • Customizable Fn buttons
  • 105.6-degree field of view

The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is a full-frame lens offering a generous 105.6-degree field of view, allowing you to capture more of the night sky. This lens naturally works with all Sony FE bodies, and if you shoot APS-C, it will give you an equivalent focal length of 24mm. This means if you currently own an APS-C camera but plan to upgrade to full-frame, this lens could comfortably join you on that journey.

As prime lenses go, this one has a few more bells and whistles than most, so there are a few more things to talk about than usual. Focusing is internal, so the front element doesn’t rotate or extend outwards, which is great when using filters.

For astrophotography, manual focus is the only way to go, but this lens also has autofocus for when you’re shooting other subjects. The autofocus isn't the fastest we’ve seen, taking about 0.25 seconds to lock onto subjects when the lens is wide open, or 0.5 seconds when stopped down. This is driven by an SMT stepping motor, which is quiet but audible.

One feature that you don’t see on many lenses is a small color digital screen on the top of the lens. This shows the focus distance, aperture setting and the active Fn control. Is it a gimmick? A bit. Is it useful? Yes. For astrophotography, the screen is definitely useful because it’s illuminated.

As with most Viltrox lenses, there’s also a USB-C port on the lens mount so it can be powered. This allows you to connect the lens to the Viltrox Lens app via Bluetooth to update firmware and customize the Fn buttons and the digital screen’s welcome screen. This makes firmware updates incredibly easy, which is a great feature to have.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: User reviews

In online reviews, users consistently highlight the lens's value and image quality. Build quality comes up time and time again, thanks to the all-metal build.

Many users report that overall, the lens offers much more than you’d expect for the price and even more than some more expensive lenses.

How we tested the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE

The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE was tested in combination with the Sony A7R V, which offers an unforgivingly high resolution. The lens was tested at night with a focus on astrophotography, and in daylight to assess sharpness, distortion and general functionality for an all-round approach to testing.

Should you buy the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE?

Buy it if:

✅ You’re on a budget: The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is less expensive than alternative lenses offering the same focal length and maximum aperture.

✅ You want a wide-angle prime: Thanks to its wide field of view, you can capture more of the night sky, while the fast maximum aperture is ideal for astrophotography.

Don't buy it if:

❌ You would like flexibility: If you would like the flexibility of a variable focal length, a zoom lens is the only way to go. They are typically slower than primes, though.

❌ You'd like a wider view: This is a lovely wide lens, but you can get wider options as both primes and zooms.

Since there are only a few alternatives to the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE, and given that it offers excellent value for money, this is absolutely a lens worth considering if you need a wide-angle prime.

Furthermore, you’ll struggle to find a similar alternative with the same balance of overall build quality and price. Image quality is excellent, even in the corners and edges of the frame when shooting wide open with minimal distortion.

The two customizable Fn buttons and the illuminated color screen that provides useful lens information are extremely helpful when shooting in the dark.

With a price of $464 (£533) and given its build quality, image quality and overall handling, this lens represents excellent value for money. And while it may be a full-frame lens, APS-C users can still enjoy a 24mm equivalent focal length, so it’s a useful lens for astrophotography whichever format you shoot with.

This is a professional-quality lens with a mid-range price tag, and like other Viltrox lenses, you get the lens, a lens hood, front and rear lens caps and a soft lens case in the box.

If this lens isn't for you

The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.2 LAB FE is a slightly less wide Viltrox lens with a much faster aperture and is part of the company’s flagship LAB series.

The Sony FE 20mm f/1.8 G is a fantastic wide-angle prime offering excellent image quality in a compact and lightweight form factor.

While space is "the final frontier," and we look outward to study everything from black holes to exploding stars, outer space can also help teach us about own planet. Satellites look back at Earth, studying its changing landforms, migrating wildlife, diminishing glaciers and natural disasters. Onboard the ISS, astronauts conduct experiments with plants, animals, microscopic organisms and an incredible amount of studies supporting human health and medical care. While space might be the final frontier, so much of the work done in space is designed to benefit us back here on Earth.

]]> <![CDATA[ When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines (and an Artemis III update) ]]> NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program.

During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon.

A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027. Artemis III will launch four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO), where they will rendezvous and dock with test versions of both companies' landers for interoperability checkouts. Those demonstrations will help inform NASA's determination about which lander the agency will choose to carry astronauts to the moon's surface on Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028.

SpaceX and Blue Origin were both awarded NASA contracts to develop HLS vehicles — Starship and Blue Moon, respectively — and have spent the past several years refining their respective lunar lander designs and dealing with various delays along the way. In the face of those delays, and in an effort to better structure its mission progression for success, NASA overhauled its Artemis program architecture in February to maintain its goal of landing astronauts on the moon by the end of 2028 and establish a more regular cadence of uncrewed landings in the meantime.

As part of that shakeup, Artemis III, previously the program's first crewed lunar landing mission, was moved up a year and repurposed for the lunar lander vehicle tests the agency is preparing to fly to LEO next year. The program's first moon landing remains scheduled for 2028, but was shifted to the manifest for Artemis IV.

Between now and then, both SpaceX and Blue Origin have more than a dozen test demonstrations and vehicle milestones to achieve, including success during Artemis III and flights afterward. This will all lead up to a key decision NASA must make: Which vehicle will carry out the first crewed landing on the surface of the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972?

Starship reached for the first time on its most recent test flight, which occurred on Sept. 28 from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. NASA lists several other important goals for the vehicle to achieve in 2026, including (in the order listed during the IAC presentation) the first return and catch of the rocket's upgraded Version 3 (V3) booster at its launch pad; the first-ever return and catch of a Ship upper stage; the first Starship launch from one of SpaceX's launch pads still under construction on Florida's Space Coast; and, possibly, the first V3 booster reflight.

NASA also expects SpaceX to complete the initial build of the crew cabin for its lunar lander Starship variant. SpaceX released renders of Starship's interior last year, as well as images of the test elevator astronauts are using to train for Starship egress on the lunar surface, but little else has been made public about the progress the company has made on the cabin's design.

Should the cabin's initial build wrap up by the end of the year, as NASA's presentation suggested, SpaceX will use Q1 2027 to complete integration of the systems that Starship will need to communicate with Orion during Artemis III, and deliver a cabin simulator for astronauts to train on leading up to the mission. SpaceX plans to continue Starship test flights through Q2 of next year, complete a landing leg demonstration and begin crew cabin airlock tests.

Blue Origin's lunar lander mockup is ready for NASA Artemis astronaut training

For Artemis III, SpaceX plans to fly one of its existing V3 Starship upper stages, with some slight modifications. Starship and Orion will dock as part of Artemis III but the SpaceX vehicle won't be equipped with a crew cabin for the mission's astronauts to enter. Between the end of this year and the beginning of the next, SpaceX is expected to complete the addition of a docking system and nosecone cover to the Artemis III Starship vehicle, which, NASA documents suggest, has already completed its mechanical fit checks.

Other notches on SpaceX's checklist leading up to Artemis III include the first propellant transfer demonstration with Starship in orbit. As the first-ever launch vehicle and spacecraft designed for full reusability, Starship's fuel constraints require that its tanks be topped off in order to fly beyond LEO. For a moon landing mission, this could mean up to a dozen launches of SpaceX's Starship "tanker" spacecraft to an orbiting fuel depot, which the moon-bound Starship will visit. To pull that off, though, SpaceX has to show it can successfully transfer those cryogenic fuels on orbit, and also store them effectively enough to prevent too much boil-off.

Starship won't require any refueling flights to complete its objectives for Artemis III, but SpaceX is expected to launch its first Starship tanker vehicle within a few months of that mission as it gears up for the Artemis IV moon landing mission. To that end, a launch of an uncrewed Starship lunar lander variant is targeted sometime toward the end of Q3/beginning of Q4, with an uncrewed lunar landing mission carried out before the end of 2027.

Blue Origin, meanwhile, has its own set of milestones to meet as it develops its Blue Moon Mark 2 (MK2) lander — a 52-foot-tall (16 meters) spacecraft powered by three BE-7 engines. Unlike the bare-bones V3 Starship that SpaceX will launch on Artemis III, Blue Origin plans to fly a completed test vehicle, incorporating the crew cabin, partial life-support, flight software and other systems needed to allow astronauts to enter the lander from Orion during their time docked in LEO. Astronauts will be able to enter Blue Moon from Orion to get a feel for the lander in zero-g and test some of its systems.

NASA's timeline shows the company working to complete a series of manufacturing and testing milestones in the last few months of 2026, including continued BE-7 testing and qualification of Blue Moon's BT-7 maneuvering thrusters. The company also faces its Artemis III interim design review and a critical design review for an upcoming landing demonstration mission in 2028.

Blue Origin is also working to restore its pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex-36 (LC-36) to operation and return its New Glenn rocket to flight, following an explosion of the rocket in May that caused extensive damage to the facility. NASA's presentation places that milestone in Q4 2026, a timeline the company has also been very vocal about maintaining. A recent Reuters report, however, suggests that may not happen until early 2027.

By early 2027, the company expects to complete the spacecraft's communications systems and finalize its flight software, with assembly, integration and testing continuing into Q2. Q1 2027 is also when Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 lander (a smaller, uncrewed version of its MK2 successor) will launch to the lunar surface as a part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program of robotic moon missions.

But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show?

The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061.

Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA. However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

Orionid shooting stars will appear to travel away from a point of origin, close to the red star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion, rising above the eastern horizon an hour before midnight for viewers in the U.S.

When and where to see Orionid shooting stars this October

Your best chance at spotting the fast-moving meteors will come in the hours before dawn on Oct. 22, after the moon has set and the radiant approaches its highest point in the night sky. It's best not to stare directly at the radiant, where the glowing meteor trails will be relatively short compared to those left by shooting stars that appear 45-90 degrees away from the bright star Betelgeuse, thanks to an effect known as foreshortening.

Try to travel away from city lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark. Always make sure someone knows where you're going if you head somewhere remote to catch the shower and be sure to take a red light to ensure that you can find your way while also preserving your night vision!

 <description>Policie zveřejnila video, v němž řidič SUV na dálnici vybrzdí a následně napadne maminku osmiletého dítěte. Na záznamu je vidět jeho zvyšující se agrese, kterou policisté odsoudili. Matka se podle nich chovala vzorně a dodržovala veškeré předpisy.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/v-kostele-v-jaromericich-nad-rokytnou-instaluji-novy-relikviar-pripomina-umucene_2610221732_elv</link>
 <description>V kostele sv. Markéty v Jaroměřicích nad Rokytnou přibyl další relikviář. Připomíná umučené kněze Jana Bulu a Václava Drbolu, v relikviáři se nachází i popel jednoho z nich. Jejich společný relikviář instaluje na místo sochař Otmar Oliva. Pojal jej jako zavěšený artefakt směřující k bronzové desce na dlažbě v boční kapli kostela.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/whatsapp_image_2026-_261022-112414_elv.jpeg?itok=VJF0tyZ4" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Český rozhlas varuje před podvodnými e-maily. Vyzývají k platbě poplatků a hrozí exekucí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/cesky-rozhlas-varuje-pred-podvodnymi-e-maily-vyzyvaji-k-platbe-poplatku-a-hrozi_2610221659_med</link>
 <description>Podvodníci se vydávají za Český rozhlas a rozesílají falešné maily s výzvou k úhradě rozhlasových poplatků. Příjemcům vyhrožují exekucí a požadují po nich zaplacení smyšlených částek. Český rozhlas kvůli tomu podá trestní oznámení. A lidem doporučuje, aby na takové zprávy vůbec nereagovali.
</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/06bd80d62d141622eed5_260616-112426_ako.jpg?itok=L_Et04Y3" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Vykázání z domova kvůli domácímu násilí na jižní Moravě přibylo. Pomáhá lepší osvěta i prevence</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/vykazani-z-domova-kvuli-domacimu-nasili-na-jizni-morave-pribylo-pomaha-lepsi_2610221615_elv</link>
 <description>V Česku přibývá případů vykázání násilníků z domácnosti i zákazů přiblížení. Podle neziskových organizací zaměřených na domácí násilí nebo stalking to automaticky neznamená, že podobných nezdravých vztahů přibývá. Nárůst souvisí i s lepší prevencí. Třeba na jižní Moravě letos policisté vykázali z bytu rekordní počet osob. </description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-034734071_191229-120247_dok.jpg?itok=eIP4uNDM" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Babiš s Juchelkou zařídili šéfce krachujícího Klokánku finanční injekci. ‚Ani zdaleka to nestačí,‘ stěžuje si</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/babis-s-juchelkou-zaridili-sefce-krachujiciho-klokanku-financni-injekci-ani_2610221610_jgr</link>
 <description>Přeplněná, podfinancovaná a s nedostatkem personálu. V takovém stavu jsou podle ředitelky Fondu ohrožených dětí Hanky Kupkové zařízení pro týrané děti. Ministr práce a sociálních věcí Aleš Juchelka (ANO) podle zjištění Radiožurnálu a iROZHLAS.cz přidal zařízením, pod která spadá i Klokánek, od nového roku 60 milionů korun navíc. Podle Kupkové to ale na pokrytí nákladů všech zařízení v České republice zdaleka nestačí. Celý systém dle ní krachuje.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/dsc_7409_260925-232201_jgr.jpg?itok=dMSFCNES" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:10:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Fotbalisté Plzně v Evropské lize přivítají Levski Sofia. Policisté i strážníci jsou v pohotovosti</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/fotbaliste-plzne-v-evropske-lize-privitaji-levski-sofia-policiste-i-straznici_2610221603_kch</link>
 <description>Viktoria Plzeň nastoupí na domácím hřišti ve čtvrtek večer od 21 hodin k mezinárodnímu zápasu proti bulharskému mistrovi Levski Sofia. Duel je vyhodnocený jako rizikový, v okolí stadionu proto budou na bezpečnost a pořádek dohlížet hlídky strážníků, ale také policisté Plzeňského a Karlovarského kraje i Prahy. Informovali o tom policejní mluvčí Ondřej Hodan a mluvčí plzeňské městské policie Jana Pužmanová.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/9b15a6b62d7ac8dd47d0cb39cd18890b.jpg?itok=5EKciIXc" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:03:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Macinka rozdal ceny za šíření dobrého jména Česka v zahraničí. Dostal ji také videoherní designér Vávra</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/macinka-rozdal-ceny-za-sireni-dobreho-jmena-ceska-v-zahranici-dostal-ji-take_2610221552_ako</link>
 <description>Režisér a herec Jiří Strach, klavírista a ředitel Pražské konzervatoře Ivo Kahánek nebo videoherní designér Daniel Vávra obdrželi ve čtvrtek v pražském Černínském paláci cenu Gratias agit za šíření dobrého jména Česka v zahraničí. Ocenění jim předal ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka (Motoristé). Celkem nyní cenu získalo 12 osobností a švýcarská Galerie Krause.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-114563003_261022-152044_ako.jpg?itok=5muycXDH" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:52:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Počet nemocných v souvislosti se salmonelózou v Újezdu už nenarůstá. Hygienici pokračují v šetření</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/pocet-nemocnych-v-souvislosti-se-salmonelozou-v-ujezdu-uz-nenarusta-hygienici_2610221523_jor</link>
 <description>V souvislosti s epidemií salmonelózy v Újezdu nad Lesy evidují pražští hygienici 494 nemocných, laboratorně potvrzených případů je 290. Počet nemocných už nenarůstá. Vyšetřování hygieniků stále pokračuje, uzavřeno bude v řádu týdnů. Ve čtvrtek o tom informovala mluvčí pražské hygienické stanice (HSHMP) Petra Batók. Radnice Prahy 21 spustila online formulář, prostřednictvím něhož je možné požádat o odškodnění.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/img_20260924_084647_260924-091324_aru.jpg?itok=iuTGDDhr" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>

   <title>Vyměnila eura a uložila velkou částku. Jak se přišlo na dobrovolnou prostituci</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-dobrovolna-prostituce-dane-ustavni-soud/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Příjmy z dobrovolné prostituce podléhají v Česku zdanění a finanční úřady mohou po poskytovatelích sexuálních služeb požadovat daň z příjmů. Rozhodl o tom Ústavní soud, který odmítl stížnost ženy, jež nechtěla uhradit doměřené daně za roky 2013 a 2014. Senát vedený soudcem Jiřím Přibáněm potvrdil závěry správních soudů, podle nichž příjmy z prostituce představují běžný ekonomický příjem a nejsou od daně osvobozeny.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:20:00 +0200</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>Hlídej si je! Nová bezplatná aplikace pomáhá ženám, jak si vyšetřit prsa</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/zdravotnictvi/zdravi-aplikace-hlidej-si-je-vysetreni-prsou/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zdravotnictvi</link>
   <description>Připomíná samovyšetření prsou, nabízí instruktážní video. Pamatuje na termín mamografického vyšetření nebo prevenci u gynekologa. Funguje například i jako menstruační kalendář. Novou aplikaci Hlídej si je! nabízí zájemkyním pacientkám organizace Bellis – pomáháme ženám s rakovinou prsu. Zdarma si ji mohou stáhnout do mobilu. Prevenci rakoviny prsu připomíná i celosvětová osvětová kampaň Růžový říjen.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Vítala migranty, teď ve Francii brání svůj obchod? Jde o lež, realita je jiná</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/evropa/vitala-migranty-ted-ve-francii-brani-svuj-obchod-jde-o-lez-realita-je-jina/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=evropa</link>
   <description>V prostředí českých i mezinárodních sociálních sítí se od konce minulého týdne masově šíří falešný příběh o francouzské „vítačce migrantů“, která prý vždy podporovala masovou migraci a teď ji zachytilo video, jak se bezmocně snaží zabránit migrantům ve vyrabování svého obchodu. K rozšíření tohoto příběhu aktivně přispěli i někteří čeští a slovenští politici. Jde ale o lež. Obchod, který mladá žena na videu brání, není vůbec její. A neexistuje ani důkaz, že by podporovala migraci.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 06:05:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/evropa/vitala-migranty-ted-ve-francii-brani-svuj-obchod-jde-o-lez-realita-je-jina/</guid>

  <item>
   <title>Pohlreich vyrazí na divoký západ. V saloonu v Plzni najde gastronomické sudoku</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/kultura/ano-sefe-zdenek-pohlreich-plzen-acw-saloon/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=kultura</link>
   <description>Steak, který se nedá ukousnout, záhadné vlčí oháňky a kuchyně vybavená domácím sporákem. Zdeněk Pohlreich tentokrát zamíří do plzeňského ACW Saloonu, kde se majitelé snaží oživit atmosféru divokého západu. Přestože je první ochutnávka téměř katastrofální, šéf si místní partu oblíbí. A nakonec pro ni připraví pořádné překvapení.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Přilepšení k důchodu 2000 korun? Senioři si musí počkat ještě několik měsíců</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-duchod-duchodci-mimoradny-prispevek-kdy-ho-dostanou-seniori-penze/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Zatímco o každoroční valorizaci v zákonném rámci mohou rozhodovat sami ministři, mimořádný příspěvek musí projít standardním legislativním procesem. Proto slíbené peníze důchodci neuvidí už v lednové výplatě penze, ale nejdříve s dvouměsíčním zpožděním. Zadlužení státu to zvýší o miliardy korun.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 04:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-duchod-duchodci-mimoradny-prispevek-kdy-ho-dostanou-seniori-penze/</guid>

    <media:description>Na mimořádný příspěvek si čeští důchodci budou muset počkat až do března. Proč? Přečtete si článek.</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Ve Francii se poprvé nakazil člověk virem Shamonda. Nemoci podlehl</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/francie-virus-shamonda-pacient-zemrel.A261022_131626_zahranicni_sile#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Francouzské zdravotnické úřady poprvé zaznamenaly virus Shamonda u člověka. Nakažený šedesátník později zemřel. Úřady ale uvedly, že v současnosti nevidí riziko pro širší populaci. Hlavní hypotézou je, že nemoc přenesl na pacienta komár na východě Francie, kde byl virus letos na jaře a v létě zaznamenán mezi zvířaty.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:45:46 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Okradl ji a peníze prohrál v sázkách. Modelka expřítele zabila jednou ranou</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/webcam-modelka-zabiti-pritel-penize-sazeni-vrazda-moskva.A261022_171225_zahranicni_fohl#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ruskou webkamerovou modelku zatkla policie poté, co údajně ubodala svého expartnera a bývalého vojáka. Ten ji okradl o více než půl milionu rublů (kolem 150 tisíc korun). Peníze následně prohrál při sportovních sázkách. </description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:36:00 GMT</pubDate>

      <media:description>Webkamerová modelka Yulia, která je obviněná z toho, že v Moskvě zavraždila svého bývalého přítele.</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Ševčík se ve Sněmovně utrhl na Šebelovou.
Vezměte si menopauzu, vzkázal jí</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/vezmete-si-menopauzu-volal-sevcik-na-sebelovou-musi-se-to-resit-mini-poslankyne.A261022_085013_domaci_jira#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>STAN i další opoziční poslanci zuří. Reagují na incident ze včerejšího pozdního jednání Sněmovny. Šéf Starostů Vít Rakušan tvrdí, že poslanec Miroslav Ševčík (SPD) častoval slovy o menopauze svoji kolegyni Michaelu Šebelovou, jež žádala o pauzu v jednání Sněmovny. Výměna názorů, do níž se podle Rakušana zapojil za použití sprostých slov i šéf Sněmovny Tomio Okamura, vyvrcholila v hádku. Okamura se podle svých slov snažil naopak situaci zklidnit.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:28:00 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Škodovka je bílá vrána, kritizoval expert zmrazení platů v celém koncernu VW</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/skoda-auto-volkswagen-zmrazeni-platu-odbory-propousteni-inflace-impuls.A261022_173938_ekonomika_linh#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Zaměstnancům Škody Auto by se měly zmrazit platy. Podle zástupců odborů KOVO to na čtyři roky požaduje koncern Volkswagen. Požadavek se má týkat také bonusů a prémií, což rovněž odboráři odmítají. „Škodovka je přitom v naprosto fantastické kondici. Ty poslední skoro dva roky je hlavní tahoun toho, co se vytváří za zisk v celé skupině Volkswagen,“ řekl ve vysílání Rádia Impuls odborník na automobilový průmysl Petr Knap.</description>

      <description>Česko porušuje právo Evropské unie, protože umožňuje výslech podezřelých bez přítomnosti obhájce v případě, že se advokát nedostaví do 48 hodin od zadržení. Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[iQCafé – Termojaderná fúze]]>

Přijďte se podívat na jednu z největších technologických výzev současnosti. Dokážeme na Zemi napodobit proces, který už miliardy let pohání hvězdy? Čeká vás poutavá přednáška o termojaderné fúzi, jejím současném stavu i vyhlídkách do budoucna.

]]> Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:51:52 GMT <![CDATA[Křišťálové Vánoce u Liebiegů]]>

Křišťálové Vánoce u Liebiegů nabídnou setkání tvůrců z Křišťálového údolí i dalších regionů na jednom místě. Čeká vás pestrá přehlídka sklářských výrobků, tradičních řemesel, autorského designu a poctivých regionálních produktů.

]]> Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:03:51 GMT <![CDATA[Café Union v České Lípě]]>

Café Union v historickém centru České Lípy zve na snídaně, obědy, výběrovou kávu a zákusky z vlastní cukrářské výroby. Kavárna zaujme interiérem laděným do secese. V patře nabízí také společenský sál pro soukromé a firemní akce.

]]> Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:49 GMT <![CDATA[Svatomartinská husa na Rychtě Jestřebí]]>

Přijďte si užít svatého Martina v klidu a pohodě k nám na Rychtu! Od 11. do 15. listopadu 2026 jsme pro vás připravili speciální sezónní menu. Všechno jsme upekli a uvěřili s láskou tak, aby vám u stolu bylo jednoduše dobře.

Ještě příští týden ale proběhnou krátkodobé uzavírky kvůli dokončovacím pracím.</description></item><item><title>Českolipské ANO opustili někteří zastupitelé, Živá Lípa spolupráci nevylučuje</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903724-ceskolipske-ano-opustili-nekteri-zastupitele-ziva-lipa-spolupraci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903724-ceskolipske-ano-opustili-nekteri-zastupitele-ziva-lipa-spolupraci.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:45:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Hnutí ANO v České Lípě opustili po volbách někteří zvolení zastupitelé. Cyklisté, buďte vidět!</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903475-se-zimnim-casem-se-stmiva-o-hodinu-driv-cykliste-budte-videt.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903475-se-zimnim-casem-se-stmiva-o-hodinu-driv-cykliste-budte-videt.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:12:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>V noci ze soboty na neděli začne platit zimní čas. Kampaň Na kole jen s přilbou připomíná, co musí mít cyklisté na kole a co jim pomůže, aby je řidiči včas viděli.</description></item><item><title>Dětské kroužky zdražují. Každá pátá rodina si je nemůže dovolit</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903664-detske-krouzky-zdrazuji-kazda-pata-rodina-si-je-nemuze-dovolit.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903664-detske-krouzky-zdrazuji-kazda-pata-rodina-si-je-nemuze-dovolit.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:55:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Michaela Pospíšilová</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Ceny dětských volnočasových aktivit rostou a rodinné rozpočty jsou pod tlakem. Projekt Darujeme kroužky dětem proto spouští kampaň, která díky individuálním dárcům pomůže dětem pokračovat v aktivitách, které je baví a rozvíjejí.</description></item><item><title>Velké pátrání na českolipském hřbitově: Vrátí se polští hrdinové konečně domů?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903661-velke-patrani-na-ceskolipskem-hrbitove-vrati-se-polsti-hrdinove-konecne-domu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903661-velke-patrani-na-ceskolipskem-hrbitove-vrati-se-polsti-hrdinove-konecne-domu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Na Městském hřbitově v České Lípě probíhá průzkum, který má odhalit přesná místa odpočinku tří polských odbojářů z roku 1945. Polští experti ve spolupráci s českým ministerstvem obrany plány exhumace koordinují tak, aby chod hřbitova nebyl nijak narušen.</description></item><item><title>Hnědé popelnice bude město vyvážet do konce listopadu, pokud nepřijde zima</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903662-hnede-popelnice-bude-mesto-vyvazet-do-konce-listopadu-pokud-neprijde-zima.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903662-hnede-popelnice-bude-mesto-vyvazet-do-konce-listopadu-pokud-neprijde-zima.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:53:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Blíží se zima a s ní i změna ve svozu bioodpadu, takzvaných hnědých popelnic. Ty se v Liberci přes zimu vyvážet vůbec nebudou, svoz potrvá jen do konce listopadu a poté se opět rozběhne pravděpodobně 1. dubna.</description></item><item><title>Pohlaďte si masožravku. V Liberci ukazují giganta bez ochranného skla</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903660-pohladte-si-masozravku-v-liberci-ukazuji-giganta-bez-ochranneho-skla.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903660-pohladte-si-masozravku-v-liberci-ukazuji-giganta-bez-ochranneho-skla.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 06:40:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Botanická zahrada Liberec láká na unikátní zážitek. V pavilonu D se zabydlela obří láčkovka Nepenthes truncata s pastmi dlouhými až 40 centimetrů. A neskrývá se za skleněnou vitrínou, uvidíte ji pěkně zblízka. Po zakořenění se jí budete moci dokonce šetrně dotknout.</description></item><item><title>Bolavá záda trápí statisíce Čechů. Kvůli páteři vyhledalo loni lékaře téměř milion lidí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903589-bolava-zada-trapi-statisice-cechu-kvuli-pateri-vyhledalo-loni-lekare-temer-milion-lidi.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903589-bolava-zada-trapi-statisice-cechu-kvuli-pateri-vyhledalo-loni-lekare-temer-milion-lidi.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 20:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Kateřina Pospěchová</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Sedavé zaměstnání v kancelářích, nedostatek pohybu a každodenní stres si vybírají svou daň. Data zveřejněná u příležitosti Světového dne páteře ukazují, že potíží dlouhodobě přibývá.</description></item><item><title>Úspěch kluka z Chrastavy. Tomáš Polák je vicemistrem světa</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903606-uspech-kluka-z-chrastavy-tomas-polak-je-vicemistrem-sveta.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903606-uspech-kluka-z-chrastavy-tomas-polak-je-vicemistrem-sveta.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 18:42:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Ostatní sporty</category><description>Mladý orientační závodník na horských kolech z Chrastavy Tomáš Polák dosáhl velkého úspěchu. Na nedávném mistrovství světa juniorů získal páté místo v individuálním závodě a stříbro ve štafetě. To ocenila i jeho mateřská Chrastava, která jej podpořila dvaceti tisíci korunami.</description></item><item><title>Soud v Liberci dostal stížnosti k volbám v Bedřichově a Slunečné</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903644-soud-v-liberci-dostal-stiznosti-k-volbam-v-bedrichove-a-slunecne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903644-soud-v-liberci-dostal-stiznosti-k-volbam-v-bedrichove-a-slunecne.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Soud v Liberci dnes dostal další dvě stížnosti k průběhu a výsledkům komunálních voleb. Jedna se týká Bedřichova a druhá Slunečné na Českolipsku, v obou žádají stěžovatelé vyslovení neplatnosti voleb. Stížností k volbám dostal zatím liberecký soud pět, termín pro jejich podání vyprší v pátek.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:11:32 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Slavnost světel https://www.vybezek.eu/296153-slavnost-svetel/ Wed, 21 Oct 2026 16:41:26 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296153 Milí přátelé spolku Thonmi z.s., rádi bychom vás pozvali na příjemnou podzimní akci, která se uskuteční v sobotu 7.listopadu 2026.

Přijďte strávit příjemné odpoledne na Asijskou poznávací stezku, kde společně oslavíme Slavnost světel a pro letošek stezku symbolicky zavřeme.

Rodiny s dětmi se od 15:30 mohou těšit na tvořivé dílny a kouzelnou procházku s lampiony osvětlenou stezkou. Nenechte si ujít vznik nádherného vzoru rangoli z barevného písku inspirovaného indickým svátkem světel – Díválí. Na zahřátí si můžete vychutnat šálek kořeněného masala čaje.

Dospělí návštěvníci se mohou zapojit do rozebírání jurty před zimou, vlhké zimní klima jí nesvědčí…

Přijďte s lampionem a můžete vzít i menší zavařovací sklenici na ozdobení, kterou si odnesete i se světýlkem.

Věříme, že společně strávíme příjemný podvečer. Těšíme se na vás!

Srdečně zve spolek Thonmi z.s.

Slavnost světel 26
